personas.description: Older first-time computer users (for example, a 76-year-old grandma).

risk_catalog.title: Unverified generated code

what_can_go_wrong.statement: Generated code can pass an initial test suite yet still be functionally incorrect.
In long verbatim data-transcription tasks, LLM-generated Python code can silently fail to preserve embedded data exactly.

guardrails: Require executable tests for generated logic before release.
Require static analysis and dependency vulnerability checks using tools that support the project's languages and package ecosystems.
Require human review before release for generated code that affects security-sensitive behavior.

evidence.title: Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot Generated Code -- A Targeted Replication Study
evidence.organization_or_author: Vahid Majdinasab, Michael Joshua Bishop, Shawn Rasheed, Arghavan Moradidakhel, Amjed Tahir, Foutse Khomh

supports_claims.basis: In the studied GitHub Copilot/Python scenarios, generated suggestions contained security vulnerabilities.

evidence.limitations: Targeted replication limited to Python, 29 scenarios across 12 CWE categories, and the studied Copilot/CodeQL versions; it does not establish vulnerability prevalence for other languages, tools, platforms, or current model versions.

evidence.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
evidence.organization_or_author: Jiawei Liu, Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yuyao Wang, Lingming Zhang

supports_claims.basis: In HumanEval+, additional tests exposed previously undetected wrong LLM-generated code that had passed the original HumanEval tests, demonstrating that generated code can pass an initial test suite yet still be functionally incorrect.

evidence.limitations: Benchmark evidence from Python function synthesis and the studied 2023 model set and test suites; it demonstrates that insufficient tests can miss functional defects, not that all generated code is wrong, that compilation success implies correctness, or that the result generalizes unchanged to every language, platform, model, project, or test strategy.

evidence.title: Verbatim Data Transcription Failures in LLM Code Generation: A State-Tracking Stress Test
evidence.organization_or_author: Mohd Ariful Haque, Kishor Datta Gupta, Mohammad Ashiqur Rahman, Roy George

supports_claims.basis: In the studied long verbatim high-precision-number transcription tasks, LLM-generated Python code could silently fail to preserve the supplied embedded data exactly.

evidence.limitations: Preprint benchmark limited to Python code generation requiring verbatim transcription of 100, 300, or 500 high-precision decimal values across 11 studied model serving tags. Evaluation uses exact-string inclusion, so numerically equivalent reformatting counts as failure. It does not establish general database, storage, hardware, or arbitrary application-data corruption, universal prevalence, or unchanged behavior for other languages, models, task types, or current systems.

risk_catalog.title: Prompt ambiguity

what_can_go_wrong.statement: Ambiguous requirements can lead to functionally divergent generated implementations.
Generated code can fail to satisfy stated constraints.
Generated-code models can fail to identify or resolve ambiguous requirements autonomously.

guardrails: Provide concrete task requirements and relevant constraints before code generation, including I/O specifications and edge-case requirements where applicable.
Require the agent to ask clarifying questions before coding when requirements are ambiguous or underspecified.

evidence.title: IntentCoding: Amplifying User Intent in Code Generation
evidence.organization_or_author: Zheng Fang, Yihong Dong, Lili Mou, Dongming Jin, Zhi Jin, Ge Li

supports_claims.basis: In the studied code-generation benchmarks, standard decoding showed degraded adherence as the number of explicit user-intent constraints increased, demonstrating that generated code can fail to satisfy stated constraints.

evidence.limitations: Peer-reviewed ACL 2026 benchmark evidence supports constraint-following failures under the studied code-generation setups, not universal failure across all models, prompts, languages, platforms, or constraint types. The inspected publication metadata/abstract does not justify labeling every omitted constraint as critical or claiming that a model wholly ignored it.

evidence.title: Assessing the Impact of Requirement Ambiguity on LLM-based Function-Level Code Generation
evidence.organization_or_author: Di Yang, Xinou Xie, Xiuwen Yang, Ming Hu, Yihao Huang, Yueling Zhang, Weikai Miao, Ting Su, Chengcheng Wan, Geguang Pu

supports_claims.basis: In the studied Orchid benchmark, evaluated LLMs frequently produced functionally divergent implementations for the same ambiguous requirement.
In the studied Orchid benchmark, evaluated LLMs could fail to identify or resolve ambiguity autonomously.

evidence.limitations: Evidence is limited to the studied function-level benchmark and evaluated models; Orchid uses ambiguity variants across lexical, syntactic, semantic, and vagueness categories, and not every ambiguity necessarily changes generated behavior. It does not establish universal failure across languages, platforms, models, interactive clarification workflows, or real-world projects.

risk_catalog.title: Unsafe handling of secrets and personal data

what_can_go_wrong.statement: Generated code can contain hard-coded credentials.
Personal data is logged or exposed.
LLM-generated Python web code can omit the Secure flag on cookies.

guardrails: Do not commit secrets to source control.
When runtime or deployment secrets are required, use a dedicated secrets-management mechanism rather than hardcoding them.
For personal data, collect only what is necessary for the application's stated purpose.
Do not record secrets or sensitive personal data directly in logs; remove, mask, sanitize, hash, or encrypt such values before logging when they are needed.
Protect sensitive data in transit with cryptographic transport protection appropriate to the protocol and threat model.
Protect stored sensitive data with cryptographic mechanisms selected according to the storage context and threat model.

evidence.title: CodexLeaks: Privacy Leaks from Code Generation Language Models in GitHub Copilot
evidence.organization_or_author: Liang Niu, Shujaat Mirza, Zayd Maradni, Christina Pöpper
evidence.version: GitHub Copilot using the studied Codex model

supports_claims.basis: In the studied GitHub Copilot/Codex setup, generated outputs exposed sensitive personal information from training data.

evidence.limitations: The study used carefully designed leakage-inducing prompt templates and a historical GitHub Copilot/Codex setup; approximately 8% (43) of the tested prompts yielded privacy leaks. It does not establish that ordinary prompts, other coding assistants, current Copilot models, all platforms, or logging behavior exhibit the same risk or prevalence.

evidence.title: Cross-Cutting Security Analysis of LLM-Generated Code via Metamorphic Testing and Association Rule Mining
evidence.organization_or_author: Zedong Peng, Chenggang Wang, Shangyue Zhu

supports_claims.basis: In the studied LLMSecEval benchmark, generated code from five open models violated the hard-coded-credentials metamorphic relation in 651 of 823 applicable snippets (79.1%).

evidence.limitations: Benchmark-derived result limited to 3,700 Python/C snippets generated from 148 LLMSecEval prompts by five studied open models and evaluated with an LLM-based judge (Claude Sonnet 4.6). It does not establish prevalence for other models, languages, platforms, ordinary production prompts, current systems, or that any hard-coded credential is a valid real-world secret or was leaked or exploited.

evidence.title: Retrieve, Refine, or Both? Using Task-Specific Guidelines for Secure Python Code Generation
evidence.organization_or_author: Catherine Tony, Emanuele Iannone, Riccardo Scandariato

supports_claims.basis: In the studied Python code-generation tasks, CodeQL-reported CWE-311 findings frequently manifested as generated cookie settings that omitted the Secure flag; the paper reports 13 such CWE-311 findings for GPT-4 under RAG and 7 for Gemini under RAG, with smaller counts in other evaluated conditions.

evidence.limitations: Peer-reviewed ICSME 2025 evidence is limited to 221 Python tasks from SecurityEval and SALLM, GPT-4, Gemini, and DeepSeek-Coder, and the studied baseline/RCI/RAG/RCI+RAG prompting setups. The reported CWE-311 issue was frequently, not universally, missing Secure cookie flags. This evidence does not establish unencrypted storage, all transport-encryption failures, prevalence in production systems, or generalization to other languages, platforms, models, or current systems.

risk_catalog.title: Inaccessible or unusable UX

what_can_go_wrong.statement: LLM-generated GUI applications can fail end-to-end interaction flows because of behavioral logic defects.
LLM-generated GUI mockups can use smaller text and abbreviated labels that reduce readability and introduce label ambiguity.
LLM-generated web code can omit alternative text needed by screen-reader users.

guardrails: Use clear, easy-to-understand language in user-facing content.
Provide clear feedback for user actions, errors, and task completion.
Provide clear step-by-step instructions for unfamiliar or error-prone workflows where needed.
Check visual contrast against applicable accessibility requirements when the interface presents visual text or controls.
Check focus order and visible focus indicators when the interface supports keyboard or keyboard-equivalent focus navigation.
Check that headings, controls, and user inputs have appropriate labels or instructions where those elements are present.
Check navigation mechanisms against applicable accessibility requirements where the interface provides navigation.
Conduct usability testing with representative actual or likely users, including novice users when they are part of the target audience, at appropriate stages throughout development.

evidence.title: Does ChatGPT Generate Accessible Code? Investigating Accessibility Challenges in LLM-Generated Source Code
evidence.organization_or_author: Wajdi Aljedaani, Abdulrahman Habib, Ahmed Aljohani, Marcelo Eler, Yunhe Feng

supports_claims.basis: In a study where 88 web developers prompted ChatGPT to generate websites, 74 of 88 generated websites had detected accessibility issues; the reported violations included missing image alt attributes, which the authors identify as important for screen-reader users.

evidence.limitations: Peer-reviewed W4A 2024 evidence is limited to ChatGPT-generated web code in the studied prompting setup and automated accessibility checks. It does not establish that every generated website lacks accessibility support, that keyboard support is generally missing, or that the result generalizes to current models, non-web platforms, or all accessibility requirements; 14 of 88 studied websites had no detected accessibility issues.

evidence.title: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
evidence.organization_or_author: Zhiyuan Peng, Wei Tao, Xin Yin, Chenhao Ying, Yuan Luo, Yiwen Guo

supports_claims.basis: In the studied repository-aware GUI code-generation benchmark, generated candidates from 10 evaluated code LLMs achieved near-zero Play@3 despite high compilation rates; Play@k requires an application to complete task-oriented end-to-end GUI playthroughs without logical errors.

evidence.limitations: FSE 2026 benchmark evidence is limited to the studied repository-aware GUI applications, languages, models, and automated LLM-based PlayTester evaluation. It does not directly measure first-time human users, beginner personas, every core user flow, all UI platforms, or current/future models. Successful generated candidates existed, and the PlayCoder repair framework improved Play@3, so this supports a possibility-scoped behavioral-flow failure rather than universal failure.

evidence.title: Qualitative Evaluation of LLM-Designed GUI
evidence.organization_or_author: Bartosz Sawicki, Tomasz Leś, Dariusz Parzych, Aleksandra Wycisk-Ficek, Paweł Trębacz, Paweł Zawadzki

supports_claims.basis: In the studied persona-adaptation experiment, an LLM-generated student-oriented GUI used smaller text and abbreviated labels; the authors report reduced readability and label ambiguity for that design.

evidence.limitations: Preprint evidence limited to 27 interactive GUI mock-ups generated with three studied models and evaluated by experts, plus a small persona-adaptation experiment. It does not establish universal unreadability, prevalence across generated interfaces, actual end-user comprehension failure, production-system behavior, every UI platform, or current/future model behavior; the same study also produced a senior-oriented variant with larger text and explicit labels.

risk_catalog.title: No release quality gate

what_can_go_wrong.statement: AI-generated code can be shipped to production without line-by-line manual verification.
AI-agent-generated Python maintenance PRs can introduce potential breaking changes.
Missing telemetry can hinder incident diagnosis and troubleshooting.

guardrails: Define required release verification checks using a risk-based approach that accounts for applicability and feasibility.
Use a staged or progressive rollout when the deployment platform supports incremental exposure and the release risk warrants it.
Maintain a documented recovery plan for unsuccessful releases, using rollback to a known good state when rollback is safe and supported, or a tested fix-forward path when it is not.
Instrument released software to emit the telemetry needed to diagnose operational failures, selecting logs, metrics, traces, or error events according to the system architecture and failure modes.
Monitor operational health using relevant telemetry signals, and configure actionable notifications for conditions that require intervention.

evidence.title: The 2026 State of AI Coding Report
evidence.organization_or_author: New Relic; survey conducted by Hanover Research

supports_claims.basis: In the 2026 Hanover Research survey commissioned by New Relic, 62% of surveyed technology leaders reported that their engineering teams often trusted AI-generated code enough to ship it to production without line-by-line manual verification.

evidence.limitations: Vendor-commissioned self-report survey of 200 U.S.-based full-time technology decision-makers in IT/Engineering at upper-mid-market and enterprise companies using generative and agentic AI in software engineering. It does not establish that the shipped code was prototype code, that every deployment lacked other quality gates, or that the result generalizes to smaller organizations, other countries, all teams, or future practice.

evidence.title: Safer Builders, Risky Maintainers: A Comparative Study of Breaking Changes in Human vs Agentic PRs
evidence.organization_or_author: K M Ferdous, Dipayan Banik, Kowshik Chowdhury, Shazibul Islam Shamim

supports_claims.basis: In the studied AIDev Python repositories, agent-generated PR patches contained statically detected potential breaking changes; maintenance-oriented refactor and chore patches had reported potential-breaking-change rates of 6.72% and 9.35%, respectively.

evidence.limitations: Peer-reviewed MSR 2026 evidence is limited to Python repositories and the AIDev dataset, and measures potential breaking changes detected from reconstructed patches with an AST-based tool rather than confirmed downstream user breakage. The study found lower potential-breaking-change rates for agentic patches than human patches overall, so this supports only a possibility-scoped maintenance-PR claim. It does not establish that breaking changes reached users, that rollback was unavailable, or that the rates generalize to other languages, repositories, agents, or current systems.

evidence.title: Observability primer

supports_claims.basis: OpenTelemetry states that observability enables troubleshooting and answering why system behavior occurs, and that applications must emit telemetry signals such as traces, metrics, and logs to support those questions; missing telemetry can therefore hinder diagnosis and troubleshooting.

evidence.limitations: Official conceptual documentation, not an empirical study of AI-generated software or a proof that incidents become impossible to diagnose. Other evidence sources can sometimes permit diagnosis even when application telemetry is incomplete; this supports `can hinder`, not the former absolute `cannot be diagnosed` wording.

minimum_requirements: Execute a functional test that verifies the product-defined core functionality against documented expected behavior.
Automate tests for documented product behaviors selected as critical based on the impact of failure on the utility's intended use, user data, privacy, or security.
When loss of user data would violate defined recovery objectives and the data cannot be acceptably reproduced from another source, maintain backups and periodically test restoration.
Protect private data from unauthorized access using controls appropriate to the application's trust boundaries, including authentication when access decisions depend on user identity.

Perform threat modeling early enough to inform security design, and revisit it when material changes to architecture, data flows, trust boundaries, or threat assumptions can change the threat analysis.
Perform risk-based security verification using applicable review, analysis, and testing techniques before release.
Use continuous integration to automatically run the project's required test suite and applicable static analysis on code changes.
Define measurable performance requirements appropriate to the product's critical workflows and operating environments, and verify them against documented acceptance criteria.
Define the accessibility requirements applicable to the product and verify conformance using the relevant standard, policy, or acceptance criteria.
Verify that released software provides the telemetry needed to diagnose operational failures and assess operational health.

Establish, communicate, and maintain incident response procedures appropriate to plausible operational and security incidents, including roles, communication, escalation, and recovery actions as applicable.
Define the supported platforms and environments, and verify compatibility across the combinations the product claims to support.
